questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Builder pattern?

options.text: Separate the step-by-step construction of a complex object from its final representation
Guarantee a class has only one instance
Create a new object by cloning an existing one
Convert one interface into another

questions.explanation: Builder is about constructing a complex object in steps. One instance = Singleton; cloning = Prototype; converting interfaces = Adapter.

questions.prompt: Builder replaces the ____ constructor smell — long, overloaded constructors with many positional parameters.
questions.explanation: The telescoping constructor (growing overloaded parameter lists) is exactly what Builder is meant to remove.

questions.prompt: In a fluent builder, why does each step method return `this`?

options.text: So the calls can be chained together
To make the object a singleton
To deep-copy the object
To hide the constructor

questions.explanation: Returning `this` lets you write builder.withA().withB().build() as one readable chain.

questions.prompt: How does Builder differ from a Factory?

options.text: A factory returns an object in one call; a builder assembles it over several named steps
They are identical
A builder can only make one instance ever
A factory always uses inheritance and a builder never does

questions.explanation: The distinguishing feature is step-by-step construction (builder) versus a single creation call (factory).

questions.prompt: What is the optional Director's job in the GoF Builder?

options.text: It runs a fixed sequence of builder steps (a reusable recipe)
It stores the single global instance
It converts the product to another interface
It notifies observers when the product changes

questions.explanation: A Director encapsulates a construction recipe so it can be reused; it's optional and often omitted.

questions.prompt: When is Builder the WRONG choice?

options.text: For a simple object with only a couple of fields
For an object with many optional parts
When you want validation centralized in build()
When you want an immutable result

questions.explanation: For simple objects a constructor or literal is clearer; Builder's ceremony only pays off for complex construction.
